review.summary:
Phase 18 is a plan-and-inventory deliverable, and I verified its claims against primary sources rather than its prose. Every one of the nine attempt-01 findings is genuinely fixed, including the blocking one: the reproduction harness now lives in the repository at `tools/g25-repro/` (covered by `review_phase.fingerprint`, which hashes tracked *and* untracked non-ignored files, tools/review_phase.py:46-48), is executed inside the gate by `python tools/g25_reproduction.py` (docs/checks/phase-18.json:73-87, exit 0, 39.6s), and asserts outcomes case-by-case in both the Rust probe (tools/g25-repro/src/main.rs:9) and the Zod script (tools/g25-repro/typescript.mts:7), so the receipt cannot silently drift from the executed experiment.

The headline factual basis of the whole 0.2.2 policy checks out against the frozen source independently of the harness: `.local/typescript/src/models/red-team.ts:566` declares `uuid: z.string()` and :1150 `created_at: z.string()` with no format refinement, while `tsg_id`/`sub_category` are required non-nullable strings and `category_display_name` is required (:567, :574, :575) — exactly matching the recorded two confirmed format mismatches and three retained strict rejections (docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json:289-325). The plan's bypass list (plan:37-38) is precisely the ten `check_string` kinds minus `min`/`max` (crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1156-1175), with an unknown-kind arm that fails closed (:1175). The request inventory reconciles exactly: 76 recorded occurrences equals my own grep of `common::uuid(` across the eight Red Team sources (2+5+3+3+8+28+15+12), extraction is now tokenizer-based and fail-closed (tools/g25_audit.py:65-67, 95-102, plus the per-file reconciliation raise at :73), and provenance is real — every recorded input digest is recomputed and asserted (tools/test_g25.py:47) and each vendor `sourceSha256` is checked before scanning (tools/g25_audit.py:64). I independently confirmed all eleven "new" operations are absent from `contracts/operations.json`, that the pinned vendor contract for target-profile error logs really exposes only `target_id` and `limit` (operations.json:3322-3347), and that the SDK freeze holds (crates/scm-sdk untouched, with the guard now extended to Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/LICENSE/NOTICE plus an untracked-file check, tools/check_phase.py:73-74).

What keeps this off a 10 is completeness of the ledger itself, which is this phase's single artifact. `fields()` silently truncates any composite kind it does not enumerate: `ZodLazy` appears nine times in `baselineFields` with no children (contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json:3636) at paths the vendor side fully expands (:391-426), and `ZodPipeline` exists in the graph and would truncate the same way. Separately, the row builder copies a key name (`unknownKeys`) that never occurs in the schema graph, so no row records `unknownFields`/`catchall` — the ledger contains zero evidence for response-policy item 3's premise that baseline objects are passthrough (I confirmed it empirically: all six `.strict()` uses in red-team.ts are request schemas, so the premise is true but unevidenced). Neither defect contradicts any stated claim — the audit's own `policy` string scopes itself to "inventory only", and the one truncated subtree resolves to identical baseline/vendor contracts when expanded by hand — so I treat them as required follow-ups rather than blockers.

findings.description: The field row builder copies `unknownKeys`, a key that never appears in the schema graph (grep for `unknownKeys` in crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json returns nothing; the graph uses `unknownFields` and `catchall`, e.g. node s010857 `"unknownFields":"passthrough","catchall":{"$ref":"s010858"}`). As a result no row in contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json records any unknown-field policy at all (grep for unknownFields/unknownKeys/catchall in audit.json returns zero matches). Response-policy item 3 at docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:53-54 rests entirely on the premise that "Baseline passthrough means new vendor fields cannot make an old operation fail", and policy item 2 selects the baseline contract as the response-mode floor, so whether each baseline and vendor object is passthrough/strip/strict is the decisive property — and the phase's headline ledger cannot answer it for any of the 47 operations. The premise does hold for this family (all six .strict() uses in .local/typescript/src/models/red-team.ts:1235-1464 are request schemas), but that is my manual check, not recorded evidence, and phase 19 would implement against an unverified assumption.
findings.required_fix: Record the object unknown-field policy in every row: copy `unknownFields` (and the `catchall` ref) instead of the nonexistent `unknownKeys`, regenerate contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json, and add a tools/test_g25.py assertion that every row with kind ZodObject carries `unknownFields` and that every paired baseline response root is `passthrough`.

findings.description: The composite dispatch enumerates ZodObject/ZodArray/ZodRecord/ZodUnion/ZodDiscriminatedUnion/ZodIntersection/ZodCatch and silently emits a childless row for every other kind, so unhandled composites truncate the field tree without any signal. This is live, not hypothetical: `ZodLazy` produces nine childless rows in `baselineFields` (contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json:3636, 3812, 4011 and the same three paths in list_jobs and get_job) whose target is a real object with required properties (schema_graph.json node s010856 -> s010857 with `code`/`name`, inputPresence "rejects"), while the vendor side of the same field is fully expanded (audit.json:391-426). `ZodPipeline` also exists in the graph (node s000040, `input`/`output` refs) and would truncate identically if it became reachable from a response root. The recursion guard at line 14 raises on recursive refs, so the tool is fail-closed there and fail-open here — the same silent-empty class of defect that attempt-01 finding 3 required be fixed for the UUID inventory. In this instance the truncated baseline subtree happens to match the vendor contract, so no claim in the plan is wrong, but the paired inventory is incomplete for 3 of the 36 paired operations.
findings.required_fix: Traverse `ZodLazy` through its `target` ref (and `ZodPipeline` through `input`/`output`), and raise ValueError for any node kind carrying child `$ref`s that is not explicitly handled, mirroring the fail-closed guard at tools/g25_audit.py:14. Regenerate the ledger and add a tools/test_g25.py assertion that no emitted row is a childless composite kind.

findings.description: ZodOptional, ZodDefault, ZodNullable and ZodBranded are all collapsed into the `optional`/`nullable` booleans of the inner node's row, so the ledger cannot distinguish a baseline optional field from a baseline defaulted field. Response-policy item 1 at docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:42 explicitly requires preserving "the distinction between defaults enabled/disabled" across Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults, and policy item 2 treats the baseline as the presence floor, yet the artifact that is supposed to document those floors erases the default marker. (The graph itself carries no default value on ZodDefault nodes, so only the marker is lost.)
findings.required_fix: Record the unwrapped wrapper chain (for example `wrappers: ["ZodOptional", "ZodDefault"]` or a `defaulted: true` flag) on each row in tools/g25_audit.py:16-17, regenerate the ledger, and assert in tools/test_g25.py that defaulted baseline fields are distinguishable from merely optional ones.

findings.description: The new project-owned Rust crate declares its own `[workspace]`, so it does not inherit the repository policy `unsafe_code = "forbid"` (Cargo.toml:12-13) that AGENTS.md:11 states for project-owned Rust, and because the root workspace members are exactly ["crates/scm-sdk"] (Cargo.toml:2) the crate is never seen by `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace` or `cargo check --workspace` in scripts/check-rust.py:61-63. It is only ever compiled by `cargo run` from tools/g25_reproduction.py:7. Its source contains no unsafe code and the file is short, but this is the same gap the phase-8 `consumer-unsafe-lint` advisory required be closed for contracts/native-probes (docs/phase-status.json:854-866).
findings.required_fix: Add `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` to tools/g25-repro/src/main.rs (or `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` to tools/g25-repro/Cargo.toml) and either rustfmt the crate or record in the plan that it is deliberately outside the formatting gate.

findings.description: The request section requires inventorying every caller-supplied UUID check and comparing it "with TypeScript's string parameters", then listing the retained checks in the changelog/compatibility report. The ledger delivers only the Rust side: `requestUuidArguments` and `requestUuidInventory` carry no paired baseline parameter type and no vendor parameter schema. The strongest justification for retaining these checks is in the pinned vendor contract itself — contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json:3327-3331 declares `target_id` as `{"type": "string", "format": "uuid"}` — and the TypeScript side carries no `.uuid(` call anywhere in .local/typescript/src/red-team/*.ts, so the comparison is true but is asserted only in prose. Phase 20 must publish this comparison from evidence.
findings.required_fix: Extend each `requestUuidArguments` entry (tools/g25_audit.py:68) to record the pinned vendor parameter schema `format` and the paired baseline parameter type, so the retained request-strictness list in the 0.2.2 changelog is derived from the ledger rather than from prose.

findings.description: Response-policy item 4 (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:63-66) names an "operation and field comparison ledger, with baseline/vendored requiredness, nullability, types, string bounds, additions and deliberate kept constraints". The committed artifact supplies the raw paired trees (`vendorFields` and `baselineFields`) and correctly links every operation to its actual response contract, but computes no diff: there is no per-operation list of vendor-added fields, no list of vendor-only constraints to be dropped, and no list of deliberately kept baseline constraints. Phase 19's generated regressions and phase 20's "document every loosened and retained rule" both need that derived view, and deriving it by hand from a 42k-line ledger is error-prone.
findings.required_fix: Emit a per-operation `comparison` section (addedVendorFields, vendorOnlyConstraints, keptBaselineConstraints) alongside the raw trees when the phase-19 work lands, and assert in tools/test_g25.py that each entry is derived from the paired trees rather than hand-listed.

findings.description: test_reproduction_and_independent_results_are_retained compares the committed cases.json to the receipt's `cases` and the recorded outcomes to the per-case expectations, but never checks the receipt's own `inputs` digests (docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json:5-11) against the committed harness files. Run in isolation, the test therefore accepts a stale receipt whose recorded run used a different src/main.rs (for example one calling parse in Mode::Request). The evidence is sound in practice only because the gate always regenerates the receipt at tools/check_phase.py:75 before running this suite, and docs/checks/ is excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:13), so the unit test is the only durable guard on the receipt's binding.
findings.required_fix: Assert in tools/test_g25.py that every path in the receipt's `inputs` map hashes to the committed file under tools/g25-repro/, mirroring the provenance assertion already present for the audit at tools/test_g25.py:47.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-18.json records seven executed checks, all exit_code 0 with captured invocations and output: git diff --check; git diff --exit-code 7f4a062 over crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE; an untracked-file guard via git ls-files --others --exclude-standard over the same paths; python tools/g25_reproduction.py (39.575s, stdout {"cases": 7, "confirmedFormatMismatches": 2}); python tools/g25_audit.py --check (stdout operations 47, jsonResponseRoots 46, matchedTypeScriptOperations 36, formatAffectedOperations 28, formatOccurrences rfc3339 56/uuid 124/duration 4, allFrozenRootsWithFormats 172, requestUuidOccurrences 76); 6 g25 tests OK; 30 review-gate tests OK. source_sha256 36c28433… matches the reviewed source and source_unchanged is true.

Attempt-01's blocking finding is resolved by relocation plus execution, not by prose: the harness is at tools/g25-repro/{Cargo.toml,Cargo.lock,cases.json,src/main.rs,typescript.mts}; tools/review_phase.py:46-48 fingerprints `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, so these untracked-but-unignored files are inside the reviewed source hash; tools/check_phase.py:75 executes them in the gate; and docs/phase-status.json:3698-3713 lists all five plus docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json in scope_evidence.

Independent confirmation of the plan's factual basis from the frozen source, without relying on the harness: .local/typescript/src/models/red-team.ts:566 `uuid: z.string()` and :1150 `created_at: z.string()` carry no format refinement (so frozen Zod accepts "opaque-service-id" and "service timestamp without RFC3339"), while :567 `tsg_id: z.string()`, :574 `sub_category: z.string()` and :575 `category_display_name: z.string()` are required non-nullable (so numeric tsg_id, null sub_category and the omitted display name are rejected). This reproduces exactly the two confirmedFormatMismatches and three retained strict cases recorded at docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json:289-325.

The plan's bypass list is exhaustive of the real validator: crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1156-1175 implements min, max, uuid, email, url, datetime, duration, date, rfc3339, regex with a fail-closed `_ => false` arm; docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:37-38 names exactly uuid, rfc3339, datetime, date, duration, email, url, regex, i.e. all format kinds and no length kind.

Request-check inventory reconciles against an independent count: my grep of `common::uuid(` across crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team gives network_broker 2, facade 5, scans 3, adapters 3, targets 8, reports 28, custom_attacks 15, custom_attack_reports 12 = 76, equal to summary.requestUuidOccurrences. Extraction is now tokenizer-based (tools/g25_audit.py:65-67, 95-102 via verify_gateway_bindings.functions/arguments, which raises on ambiguous names at verify_gateway_bindings.py:52), raises on a missing audited method (:66) and on any call site with an argument count other than one (:100), and reconciles per-file totals against per-method sums (:73).

Provenance is now actual and verified: contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json:4-23 lists the 18 files really read (vendor operations.json, contracts/operations.json, both red-team mapping files, contracts/manifest.json, schema_graph.json and the eleven Red Team Rust sources), contracts/typescript.json is gone, tools/test_g25.py:44-47 recomputes every digest and asserts typescript.json is absent, and tools/g25_audit.py:64 rejects a stale vendor sourceSha256 before scanning (verified against operations.json:3320 for facade.rs).

Classification of the eleven unpaired operations is correct: contracts/operations.json contains no reports-client getStatus/regenerate/ASR/override entries (only downloadReport, generatePartialReport, getAttackDetail, getDynamic*/getStatic*, getStreamDetail, listAttacks, listGoals, listGoalStreams) and no scans-client setRuntimeProfile (only abort, create, get, getCategories, list, listAll), so v1 download_report pairs and v2 get_download_url does not. The CSV operation now carries its explicit label (audit.json:38299-38300 responseRoot null with responseHandling "csv_bytes").

Query-behavior claims match the pinned vendor contract: contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json:3322-3347 exposes only target_id (path, format uuid) and limit (query, 1-100, default 5) for get_target_profile_error_logs, and the ledger records rejectedQueryOptions {skip, search} with requestUuidArguments [target_id], asserted at tools/test_g25.py:14-18.

The ledger completeness gaps I found: grep for `unknownKeys` in crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/schema_graph.json returns nothing while node s010857 carries `"unknownFields":"passthrough"`, and grep for unknownFields/catchall in contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json returns zero matches; nine childless `ZodLazy` rows appear in baselineFields (audit.json:3636, 3812, 4011 plus the same three paths under list_jobs and get_job) whose target s010857 has required `code`/`name`, while the vendor side of that field is expanded at audit.json:391-426.

Governance artifacts are consistent: docs/PHASES.md:88-94 adds the G25 section with the typo corrected ("Version 0.2.1 remains"), docs/implementation-plan.md:166-172 adds the missing follow-up section, docs/phase-status.json:3715-3720 records the attempt-01 disposition, and docs/reviews/phase-18-attempt-01.{json,prompt.md,cli.json} are preserved with gate_passed false at score 8.
limitations: Read-only review with no Bash: I did not execute tools/g25_audit.py, tools/g25_reproduction.py, the Rust probe, the Zod script or any unittest suite. All check results were read from docs/checks/phase-18.json and docs/checks/phase-18-reproduction.json, which record real invocations, exit codes, durations and raw stdout, and I could not recompute the recorded SHA-256 digests. Where it mattered I re-derived the underlying facts from primary sources (frozen Zod schemas, the vendor OpenAPI operations file, the Rust validator, grep counts of common::uuid) rather than relying on the recorded outputs.

I verified the pairing logic and about six of the 47 operation records in depth (create_job, list_jobs, get_job for the ZodLazy gap; get_target_profile_error_logs; download_error_logs; download_report v1/v2) plus all eleven new-operation classifications and the 36/11 split. The remaining per-field vendor/baseline pairings were checked structurally and at the summary level, not field by field.

The 172-root global format inventory was checked for method soundness (tools/g25_audit.py:75-91 walks every `$ref` in each non-vendor root, so it is strictly more complete than the per-operation `fields()` traversal) and for the count recorded in the gate output, but I did not enumerate or spot-check individual non-Red-Team roots.

The consumer's 17 reported loopback failures remain unexecuted and unverifiable here; the plan states the checkout is on an unreachable host and explicitly forbids claiming those tests ran. I treated that as honestly disclosed, not as evidence. Likewise no live service acceptance is claimed or established by this phase.

Reproducibility of the independent Zod half depends on the external .local/typescript checkout and its node_modules, which are outside the repository; the gate binds it through `tools/verify-contracts.py --baseline .local/typescript` (recorded verified at baseline 0.34.0, commit 4a80dbdb, extractedBaselineVerified true) rather than by committing the baseline. I inspected .local/typescript only as the permitted frozen reference and read no credential or tenant-registration files; I made no network calls and modified nothing.

I judged milestone 18 only (plan, paired inventory, retained reproduction, audit/review-tool guards, SDK freeze). The validator change, mode-aware contract selection, generated typed fallback, per-operation Zod-derived regressions, CI wiring, packaging and publication are phase 19 and 20 obligations and are not treated as missing here; phase 18's gate also does not run the full cumulative suite, so I cannot rule out interactions between the new tools/g25-repro crate and checks that only phases 19-20 execute.
